reviews.body:
Thanks for fixing the cache-token gap in `PostHog.Integrations.LLMAnalytics.Req`! The core Anthropic and OpenAI token extraction looks clean, and local validation (`mix format --check-formatted`, `mix credo --strict`, `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`, `mix posthog.public_api --check`, `mix test` — 1104/1104, and an end-to-end smoke check capturing synthetic Anthropic/OpenAI/OpenRouter `$ai_generation` events through `sdk-mock-server`) passed.

Two concerns around how `$ai_cache_reporting_exclusive: false` is emitted on OpenAI-shaped responses are noted inline:
1. Emitting `false` unconditionally overrides PostHog ingestion's `provablyExclusive` guard when an OpenAI-compatible provider reports exclusive counts (`input_tokens < cache_read + cache_creation`), producing negative input costs.
2. Emitting `false` overwrites caller-supplied `$ai_cache_reporting_exclusive` overrides passed via `PostHog.LLMAnalytics.start_span/2` or `PostHog.set_context/2` (which worked prior to this PR and are preserved by `posthog-js` and `posthog-python`).

Also left two minor optional suggestions inline on OpenAI boundary tests and changeset wording.

Thanks for the quick follow-up! Both concerns (`input_tokens >= cache_total` guard for exclusive OpenAI-compatible providers like `xiaomi/mimo-v2.5`, and preserving caller-supplied atom/string `$ai_cache_reporting_exclusive` overrides from span and `$ai_generation` context) and both suggestions (OpenAI zero/nil/write-only boundary tests and changeset wording) are cleanly addressed.

Re-validated locally on `90b64c9b` (`mix format --check-formatted`, `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`, `mix posthog.public_api --check`, `mix credo --strict`, `mix test` — 1115/1115, and an 8-scenario synthetic Anthropic/OpenAI/OpenRouter `$ai_generation` smoke test through `sdk-mock-server`). Looks good to merge once GitHub Actions CI passes.

review_comments.body:
**Concern:** `put_openai_cache/2` unconditionally sets `:"$ai_cache_reporting_exclusive" => false` whenever OpenAI-style cache tokens are present, which defeats PostHog ingestion's `provablyExclusive` guard and causes negative `$ai_input_cost_usd` when an OpenAI-compatible provider reports exclusive counts (`input_tokens < cache_read + cache_creation`) or non-integer `input_tokens`.

In `PostHog/posthog` (`nodejs/src/ingestion/pipelines/ai/costs/input-costs.ts:56-75`, added in PR #74183), `resolveCacheReportingExclusive` returns an explicit boolean `$ai_cache_reporting_exclusive` immediately before running the `provablyExclusive = inputTokens < cacheReadTokens + cacheWriteTokens` fallback (tested in `input-costs.test.ts:164-193`, e.g., `xiaomi/mimo-v2.5` with `prompt_tokens: 149` and `cached_tokens: 23104`). When `exclusive` is forced to `false` on such an event, `calculateInputCost` (`input-costs.ts:243-267`) subtracts `cached_tokens` from `input_tokens` without clamping (since `clampTextTokens` only clamps when modality tokens are present), producing a negative uncached token count and negative `$ai_input_cost_usd`.

- **Base (`5d374788`) vs Head (`54a07c3b`):** Verified in ExUnit with `xiaomi/mimo-v2.5` (`prompt_tokens: 149`, `prompt_tokens_details: %{"cached_tokens" => 23_104}`): Base emits `%{"$ai_input_tokens": 149}` (no exclusive flag), whereas Head emits `%{"$ai_input_tokens": 149, "$ai_cache_read_input_tokens": 23104, "$ai_cache_reporting_exclusive": false}`.
- **Impact:** Any OpenAI-compatible provider/model using exclusive counting (with `input_tokens < cache_total`) billed through `PostHog.Integrations.LLMAnalytics.Req` receives negative input costs in PostHog instead of being rescued by the backend fallback. Standard inclusive OpenAI and OpenRouter-Claude calls are unaffected because inclusive counts always satisfy `input_tokens >= cache_read + cache_creation`.

Consider guarding the flag so it is only emitted when `input_tokens` can actually contain the reported cache tokens (aligning with the backend `provablyExclusive` contract while preserving the exact behavior for all inclusive responses):

```elixir
defp put_openai_cache(properties, details) when is_map(details) do
  props =
    properties
    |> put_cache_read(details["cached_tokens"])
    |> put_cache_creation(details["cache_write_tokens"])

  input_tokens = Map.get(props, :"$ai_input_tokens")

  cache_total =
    Map.get(props, :"$ai_cache_read_input_tokens", 0) +
      Map.get(props, :"$ai_cache_creation_input_tokens", 0)

  if cache_total > 0 and is_integer(input_tokens) and input_tokens >= cache_total do
    Map.put(props, :"$ai_cache_reporting_exclusive", false)
  else
    props
  end
end
```

Consider adding a regression test in `test/posthog/integrations/llm_analytics/req_test.exs`:

```elixir
test "omits $ai_cache_reporting_exclusive when OpenAI-compatible cache tokens exceed input tokens",
     %{req: req} do
  Req.Test.expect(@mock_module, fn conn ->
    Req.Test.json(conn, %{
      "choices" => [],
      "model" => "xiaomi/mimo-v2.5",
      "usage" => %{
        "completion_tokens" => 9,
        "prompt_tokens" => 149,
        "prompt_tokens_details" => %{"cached_tokens" => 23_104}
      }
    })
  end)

  Req.post!(req, url: "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions", json: %{messages: []})

  assert [%{properties: properties}] = all_captured(@supervisor_name)
  assert properties[:"$ai_input_tokens"] == 149
  assert properties[:"$ai_cache_read_input_tokens"] == 23_104
  refute Map.has_key?(properties, :"$ai_cache_reporting_exclusive")
end
```

**Concern:** Emitting `:"$ai_cache_reporting_exclusive" => false` here silently overwrites caller-supplied `$ai_cache_reporting_exclusive` overrides set via `PostHog.LLMAnalytics.start_span/2` or `PostHog.set_context/2` (and produces duplicate atom+string keys if the caller uses a string key).

Because `capture_generation/1` (`lib/posthog/integrations/llm_analytics/req.ex:165-175`) calls `LLMAnalytics.capture_current_span/3` (`lib/posthog/llm_analytics.ex:370`: `pop_span |> Map.merge(properties)`), and `PostHog.capture/3` (`lib/posthog.ex:186-189`) merges `get_event_context |> Map.merge(properties)`, `Req`'s extracted map wins over both span and process context. While that merge order is pre-existing for response-fact fields like `$ai_model`, `$ai_cache_reporting_exclusive` is explicitly documented as a caller override ([calculating-costs docs](https://posthog.com/docs/ai-observability/calculating-costs) — "Overriding auto-detection"), and both `posthog-js` (`packages/ai/src/openai/capture.ts:23-41`) and `posthog-python` (`posthog/ai/openai_agents/processor.py:594`, `utils.py:165`) ensure caller-supplied `$ai_cache_reporting_exclusive` takes precedence.

- **Base (`5d374788`) vs Head (`54a07c3b`):** Verified in ExUnit against an OpenAI Chat Completions response (`prompt_tokens: 100`, `cached_tokens: 64`):
  - `LLMAnalytics.start_span(sup, %{"$ai_cache_reporting_exclusive": true})` -> Base: `true`; Head: `false` (overwritten).
  - `PostHog.set_context(sup, %{"$ai_cache_reporting_exclusive": true})` -> Base: `true`; Head: `false` (overwritten).
  - `LLMAnalytics.start_span(sup, %{"$ai_cache_reporting_exclusive" => true})` -> Base: `"$ai_cache_reporting_exclusive" => true`; Head: both `:"$ai_cache_reporting_exclusive" => false` and `"$ai_cache_reporting_exclusive" => true` present in the same map.
- **Impact:** Callers talking to an OpenAI-compatible provider that uses exclusive reporting (especially when `input_tokens >= cache_total`, where backend auto-detection cannot infer exclusivity) cannot override the accounting flag per-call via `start_span/2` or `set_context/2` (the documented property hooks for `Req`), leaving only a global `before_send` callback.

Consider aligning with `posthog-js` and `posthog-python` by checking the popped span and `$ai_generation` context in `capture_generation/1` and omitting `Req`'s inferred `:"$ai_cache_reporting_exclusive"` when the caller already set `:"$ai_cache_reporting_exclusive"` or `"$ai_cache_reporting_exclusive"` (no public API change needed):

```elixir
defp capture_generation({request, response_or_exception}) do
  supervisor = request.options[:posthog_supervisor] || PostHog
  properties = Req.Request.get_private(request, @properties_key, %{})
  span = LLMAnalytics.pop_span(supervisor)
  context = PostHog.get_event_context(supervisor, "$ai_generation")

  properties =
    if has_cache_exclusive_override?(span) or has_cache_exclusive_override?(context) do
      Map.delete(properties, :"$ai_cache_reporting_exclusive")
    else
      properties
    end

  PostHog.capture(supervisor, "$ai_generation", Map.merge(span, properties))

  {request, response_or_exception}
end

defp has_cache_exclusive_override?(map) do
  Map.has_key?(map, :"$ai_cache_reporting_exclusive") or
    Map.has_key?(map, "$ai_cache_reporting_exclusive")
end
```

Consider adding regression tests in `test/posthog/integrations/llm_analytics/req_test.exs`:

```elixir
test "preserves caller-supplied $ai_cache_reporting_exclusive from start_span", %{req: req} do
  Req.Test.expect(@mock_module, fn conn ->
    Req.Test.json(conn, %{
      "choices" => [],
      "model" => "custom-model",
      "usage" => %{
        "completion_tokens" => 9,
        "prompt_tokens" => 100,
        "prompt_tokens_details" => %{"cached_tokens" => 64}
      }
    })
  end)

  LLMAnalytics.start_span(@supervisor_name, %{"$ai_cache_reporting_exclusive": true})
  Req.post!(req, url: "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions", json: %{messages: []})

  assert [%{properties: properties}] = all_captured(@supervisor_name)
  assert properties[:"$ai_cache_reporting_exclusive"] == true
end
```

**Suggestion:** Consider adding boundary tests under `describe "cache token usage"` for:
1. OpenAI responses with zero/nil cache details (explicitly asserting `refute Map.has_key?(properties, :"$ai_cache_read_input_tokens")`, `refute Map.has_key?(properties, :"$ai_cache_creation_input_tokens")`, and `refute Map.has_key?(properties, :"$ai_cache_reporting_exclusive")`; the existing Responses test at lines 192-248 uses a partial map match that wouldn't catch extra keys).
2. Write-only OpenAI-compatible usage (`cache_write_tokens > 0` with `cached_tokens: 0` or absent), including on OpenAI Responses `input_tokens_details`.

This locks in the conditional omission and `or` branch in `put_openai_cache/2` (`lib/posthog/integrations/llm_analytics/req.ex:382-386`) against future refactors.

**Suggestion:** Consider also mentioning OpenAI-compatible `cache_write_tokens` (`$ai_cache_creation_input_tokens`) and `$ai_cache_reporting_exclusive: false` in the changeset so the generated changelog reflects all newly emitted properties:

> LLM analytics events captured by the Req integration now include `$ai_cache_read_input_tokens` and `$ai_cache_creation_input_tokens` for Anthropic and OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions and Responses APIs (along with `$ai_cache_reporting_exclusive: false` for inclusive OpenAI-shaped responses), so cached input tokens are priced correctly.

comments.body:
Thanks for the detailed review. Pushed two commits addressing both points: `$ai_cache_reporting_exclusive: false` is now only emitted when `input_tokens >= cache_read + cache_creation` (so exclusive-count providers fall through to the backend `provablyExclusive` guard), and it is omitted when the caller already set the property (atom or string key) on the span or in the `$ai_generation` context. Added regression tests for the xiaomi/mimo case and for span/context/string-key overrides. Also added the boundary tests (zero/nil cached tokens on Chat Completions and Responses, write-only `cache_write_tokens` with zero or absent `cached_tokens` on both APIs) and updated the changeset with your wording plus the OpenAI-compatible `cache_write_tokens` and `$ai_cache_reporting_exclusive: false` behaviour.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
